title: My AI game dev workflow: 100% AI prototype, ~30% AI by the demo, and I still own the engine
author: WritingDecent9543
selftext:
Here's the workflow I use, from idea to demo:



1. One idea + a rough system sketch.

2. All-in AI prototype: docs, art, music and code are 100% AI.

3. Polish the prototype: cut what isn't fun or isn't needed, add elements with orthogonal design. Still 100% AI, but this stage outputs the inputs for the next one: a demo plan, prototype Aseprite files, audio + interactive music rules, and all text as i18n CSV/JSON.

4. Human polish, following the plan: hand-polished Aseprite art, sound and interactive music. Art and audio drop to \~30% AI. Translation goes to a third-party vendor at \~70% AI (AI handles the basics and UI text well, but a human review is still worth it).

5. Code stays 100% AI, but the engine, architecture and project structure underneath are designed by me. That foundation is what makes it work. If you're proud of hand-writing business code, why not write your own OS first?



The full release is just another loop of the same process with new content.



Curious how others split it: what's your AI % per discipline right now, and where do you pull humans back in?
